title: Generative Adversarial Nets
blurb: Trained a generator by pitting it against a discriminator that learns to tell real samples from generated ones, with no likelihood and no Markov chains.
intro: The discriminator is a binary classifier trained with cross-entropy on real and generated samples; the generator is trained to make the discriminator wrong. The two alternate, usually with a few discriminator steps per generator step, and the paper's practical trick is the non-saturating generator loss. The steps build the networks, the classifier loss and a single adversarial update; the capstone runs the full alternating loop on 1-D data and also asks how to evaluate the result.
